Case Study: Filling a Reservoir

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A municipal reservoir is being refilled after maintenance. Engineers monitor the inflow and model the rate at which water enters as r(t)=3t²+2, measured in thousand litres per hour, where t is the number of hours since pumping began. Because the rate keeps rising, the volume added is not simply rate times time; instead the total water collected over an interval equals the area under the rate–time graph, obtained by integrating r(t). The team wants several figures for its report: how much water enters during the first two hours, how much more arrives between the second and fourth hours, and the average inflow rate across the full four-hour session. Each of these is a definite integral of the same rate function taken over different limits of integration.
